status_definitions.validated: An authentic data product, or a direct geometric derivative of one (slope, profile) at a scale the data resolve, with a published accuracy assessment.
status_definitions.exploratory: Computed by MarsShield with a model that has not been tested against measurements in this region.
status_definitions.unavailable: Not offered here; the reason is stated.

raw_inputs.note: Olympus Mons caldera window at native resolution and a 1/8 overview of the volcano, read by HTTP range requests

regions.name: Gale Crater
regions.summary: Curiosity's radiation measurements and the terrain around Mount Sharp.

capabilities.name: Elevation, 3D terrain
capabilities.detail: USGS MSL Gale merged DEM, 1 m.

capabilities.name: Radiation measurements
capabilities.detail: Curiosity RAD Level 2 dose rates (NASA PDS/SPDF) at 322 stops.

capabilities.name: Terrain shielding model (RAD-E)
capabilities.detail: Tested retrospectively against RAD (322 stops, 8 parking periods). Its albedo share was derived from the same data, so this is not independent validation.

capabilities.name: Three-region dose comparison
capabilities.detail: The same published-table model as Jezero and Olympus Mons, at the MCD pressure; a different quantity from the RAD-E product above.

capabilities.name: Routes and where to stand
capabilities.detail: Planning illustration from the RAD-E model; not validated for astronaut dose and not for operational use.

regions.name: Mars
regions.summary: Global elevation from the Mars Global Surveyor laser altimeter.

capabilities.name: Global elevation
capabilities.detail: MOLA gridded elevations at about 15 km per pixel; finer features are not resolved.

capabilities.name: Three-region dose comparison
capabilities.detail: Effective dose, dose equivalent and water-phantom absorbed dose at Gale, Jezero and Olympus Mons from one published transport model (Zhang et al. 2022) and one atmosphere source (Mars Climate Database v6.2), at matched assumptions. Reproduced from published tables; not validated outside Gale.

capabilities.name: Global radiation map
capabilities.detail: Only three sites have matched atmospheric inputs here; a global map would need the full MCD and transport tables over every location.

regions.name: Jezero Crater
regions.summary: Perseverance's landing site and traverse on the USGS Mars 2020 CTX elevation model.

frame.note: x = R cos(lat_c) dlon, y = R dlat on the 3,396,190 m sphere; east-west scale error within +/-0.3 % across the region

capabilities.name: Elevation, 3D terrain
capabilities.detail: USGS Mars 2020 CTX DTM, 20 m posts.

capabilities.name: Slope and elevation profiles
capabilities.detail: Over 20 m (profiles on the 60 m grid). Steps, boulders and scarps narrower than about 40 m are not resolved, so this cannot judge traversability.

capabilities.name: Perseverance traverse
capabilities.detail: Localized waypoints (NASA/JPL); the DTM agrees with the rover elevations to a median of about 1 m.

capabilities.name: Sky blocked by terrain
capabilities.detail: Same definition as Gale, on the 60 m grid; misses walls narrower than about 100 m.

capabilities.name: Surface pressure
capabilities.detail: MEDA pressure (PDS), normalised to the landing elevation, agrees with the Mars Climate Database annual mean to about 0.5 %; the model uses MCD for consistency with the other sites.

capabilities.name: GCR dose estimate
capabilities.detail: Effective dose, dose equivalent and water-phantom absorbed dose from published AtRIS/Geant4 tables at the MCD pressure. No ionizing-radiation detector has operated at Jezero, so the estimate cannot be validated here.

capabilities.name: Dose differences across the region
capabilities.detail: Hydrostatic pressure from the DTM; the modeled change across the region is within the scatter of the published tables, so the model gives no meaningful distinction between locations.

capabilities.name: Terrain shielding of dose
capabilities.detail: The published tables have no zenith-angle resolution, so blocked sky cannot be turned into dose without an invented factor.

capabilities.name: RAD-E comparison, walking routes
capabilities.detail: No RAD-equivalent measurement or detector model exists for Jezero; the 20 m DTM cannot represent walking-scale hazards.

regions.name: Olympus Mons caldera
regions.summary: The summit caldera of the largest volcano on Mars, with the USGS geologic map of its six paterae.

frame.note: x = R cos(lat_c) dlon, y = R dlat on the 3,396,190 m sphere; east-west scale error within +/-0.6 % across the map

capabilities.name: Elevation, 3D caldera
capabilities.detail: HRSC/MOLA blend at 200 m posts over the 1:200,000 map area.

capabilities.name: Slope and elevation profiles
capabilities.detail: Over 200 m only. Caldera walls 1–3 km high are steeper over shorter distances than this shows.

capabilities.name: Geologic units
capabilities.detail: USGS SIM 3470 polygons (Mouginis-Mark, 2021), 1:200,000.

capabilities.name: Surface pressure
capabilities.detail: Mars Climate Database v6.2 only; no pressure has been measured above about 4 km anywhere on Mars. A ±10 % assumption band is shown.

capabilities.name: GCR dose estimate
capabilities.detail: Effective dose, dose equivalent and water-phantom absorbed dose from published AtRIS/Geant4 tables; the paper's 82 Pa case is the top of Olympus Mons. No measurement exists here.

capabilities.name: Dose differences across the caldera
capabilities.detail: Hydrostatic pressure from the DEM; the modeled change across the caldera is within the scatter of the published tables.

capabilities.name: Terrain shielding of dose
capabilities.detail: No zenith-angle resolution in the published tables, and a 200 m grid cannot locate person-scale shelter.

capabilities.name: RAD-E comparison, walking routes
capabilities.detail: No RAD-equivalent model at 2–3 g/cm2; the 200 m grid cannot represent hazards at the scale of a person.
